item.title: Indiana legal secretary faces 42 felonies over alleged fake court orders and stolen client fees
item.description: Following a lengthy three-year investigation, Heather Ann Textor, a legal secretary, has been taken into custody for alleged fraudulent activities. She is accused of forging court documents and misappropriating client funds intended for legal fees. The investigation was sparked when a local resident submitted a counterfeit expungement petition to the state police, leading to further scrutiny of suspicious transactions that funneled money into Textor's personal accounts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: John Oliver bought $15 million in medical debt for $60,000, then erased bills for 9,000 people
item.description: In June 2016, John Oliver's show made headlines by acquiring nearly $15 million of unpaid medical debt for only $60,000. This debt was funneled through a newly established company aimed at giving it away. Rather than pursuing payments, the debt was assigned to a nonprofit dedicated to alleviating medical debt, drawing attention to critical flaws in the American healthcare system.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Missouri woman accused of pointing gun at neighbour during property-line dispute
item.description: A dispute over property lines in St. Charles County turned alarming when a neighbour was allegedly shot at. Facing felony charges, Paula Kohensky is at the center of this escalation tied to a fence repair matter. The ongoing tension between the neighbours is highlighted by surveillance footage that contradicts her version of events. A preliminary hearing is set for December 2, as the case unfolds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rare hawks nest in California county after 30 years as abandoned farmland gets a new life
item.description: A California floodplain restoration project launched in 2023 has recorded its first confirmed nesting Swainson’s hawks in Shasta County in about 30 years. More than 32,000 native trees and plants were introduced across 150 acres of damaged land near the Sacramento River. Conservationists have also recorded rare indigo buntings breeding at the site, raising hopes for wildlife recovery.

item.title: Indiana father leaves everything to fiancee; daughter's failed fight leaves her with $22,208 bill
item.description: An Indiana woman who challenged her late father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her legal battle. Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208 in attorney fees after failing to prove the will was invalid. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the ruling and ordered her to pay additional legal fees after finding serious problems with her appeal.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2023, California moved 246 endangered abalone; by 2026, counts rose from 54 to 302, with juveniles found
item.description: In 2023, researchers relocated 246 black abalone to a protected coastal site to encourage population growth. After three years, surveys recorded an increase in individuals from 54 to 302, showing signs of recovery. Juvenile abalone were also found, which raises hopes for future reproduction. This project involved collaboration among several scientific organizations and demonstrated the feasibility of habitat restoration. Ongoing monitoring will be crucial to determine the population's long-term sustainability.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: London woman loses boundary dispute over 48cm strip of land claimed by neighbours
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, a homeowner in Surbiton, London, lost a legal dispute concerning a narrow 48-centimetre strip of land. It was determined that the neighbours' kitchen extension had effectively claimed squatters' rights, having occupied the land uncontested for over two decades. The First-tier Tribunal's decision highlights crucial insights into property borders and emphasizes the importance of diligent title plan checks for prospective buyers to avoid future complications.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan father's free Halloween display draws 18,000 visitors, sparks dispute with city officials
item.description: Nate Taylor launched Dead Ends on Spruce, a Halloween experience dedicated to families seeking a safe and fun outing. The festive display, equipped with animatronics and eerie soundscapes, started after an ad for complimentary decorations. Despite legal hurdles imposed by city officials, Taylor persevered. Last October, the event delighted around 18,000 visitors and provided special sessions for children with special needs, emphasizing inclusivity in community celebrations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Eva Longoria’s $55,000 fund for six women grows to $525,000 in loans, supporting 150 jobs
item.description: Eva Longoria’s foundation and nonprofit lender Accessity launched a $55,000 loan fund in 2013 to help six Latina entrepreneurs start or grow their businesses. Since then, the initiative has facilitated 65 loans worth nearly $525,000 and helped create or maintain 150 jobs. A new three-year, $500,000 grant will expand business training and financial support for Latina entrepreneurs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lost Eloise portrait found in dumpster sells for $100,000 after decades in closet
item.description: In a fascinating twist of fate, Eloise's original portrait, crafted by Hilary Knight in 1956, mysteriously disappeared during a Junior League Ball in 1960. Rediscovered in a dumpster, it lay dormant in Knight's closet for years, only to be brought back to life at a 2017 exhibition at the New-York Historical Society. Its subsequent auction at Bonhams in 2018 for $100,000 underscores the unpredictable journey and enduring value of art.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Insurer denies heart procedure for 12-year-old with Kawasaki disease
item.description: Rowan Lowry, a 12-year-old boy, urgently needs a stent procedure to address complications stemming from Kawasaki disease. His family faces an insurance denial categorizing the procedure as medically unnecessary. Undeterred, they plan to seek treatment at Boston Children's Hospital, driven by their concern for Rowan's deteriorating health and the fear of open-heart surgery. Determined, they vow to advocate fiercely for their son's well-being despite the financial strain.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teen Builds Rural Stem Access: Ontario student launches Project RISE; initiative widens STEM opportunities
item.description: At just 17 years old, Amara Wilson-Zegil is on a mission to bridge the gap in STEM education for children in rural areas. With an impressive outreach to over 1,800 students through robotics initiatives and camps, she has launched Project RISE. This groundbreaking initiative aims to combat educational disparities by providing vital tech experiences, ensuring more youth in Northern Ontario can access quality STEM opportunities.

item.title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
item.description: Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 and send its first astronaut for a space mission. The astronaut, selected from candidates trained in China, is expected to participate in scientific experiments. Cooperation with China enhances Pakistan's aspirations in space exploration and technological advancement. Additionally, plans for establishing the first Space Museum at the University of Narowal were announced to promote scientific awareness.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Brazilian man sells all, travels 1,200 miles to marry online girlfriend, discovers she was AI-generated
item.description: A Brazilian man sold all his belongings and travelled over 1,200 miles to meet the online girlfriend he hoped to marry. Edimar Martins, 49, discovered that the woman, featured on a TikTok account with around 300,000 followers, was AI-generated. After running out of money, he received assistance to return home but remains hopeful about finding love.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida opens $191.8M water plant to protect the Matanzas River and conserve drinking water
item.description: St. Johns County Utilities officials celebrated the completion of the State Road 207 Water Reclamation Facility. This facility, costing $191.8 million, will treat wastewater and provide reclaimed water for irrigation purposes. The project aims to reduce dependence on the Floridan Aquifer, especially during ongoing drought conditions. Capacity of the facility can be expanded to meet future demand while preventing nutrient pollution in local waters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida appeals court overturns $2,675 monthly alimony after a 249-day marriage
item.description: A recent decision by a Florida appeals court reversed an alimony order for a short marriage lasting 249 days. The court found insufficient evidence regarding the former wife's need for financial support. The trial court had awarded nine months of temporary alimony based on prior cases instead of specific proof. The appeals court emphasized the importance of individual cases and relevant evidence in such rulings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: Egypt announced its willingness to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia to ensure its security and stability. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi convened the National Defence Council to discuss potential support amid Houthi assaults. These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited.
